text: Lesson 11 talked about a controller tracking broker liveness and driving leader election. For most of Kafka's history, ZooKeeper made that possible — a separate coordination system, not part of Kafka itself.
ZooKeeper stored cluster metadata, elected the controller broker, and detected failures. That worked, but every Kafka cluster was really two systems to run and operate.
KRaft replaces ZooKeeper with consensus built directly into Kafka. A small set of brokers take on a controller role and agree on metadata among themselves — no external system.
In KRaft mode, brokers declare broker and controller roles, and a quorum of voters replaces the ZooKeeper ensemble. As of Kafka 4.0, KRaft is the only supported mode.
One less external system between you and a working cluster. Next up: Schema Registry, closing out this chapter.
